questions.q: What is the correct three-level hierarchy in the General Ledger journal model?
questions.explain: A batch groups one or more journal headers, and each header owns its own set of debit/credit lines.

questions.q: What does a GL_JE_LINES row's CODE_COMBINATION_ID identify?
options: The supplier who submitted the invoice
The specific chart-of-accounts combination the line posts to
questions.explain: CODE_COMBINATION_ID points to the exact account combination (company, cost center, natural account, etc.) that line hits.

questions.q: What is the difference between ENTERED_DR/ENTERED_CR and ACCOUNTED_DR/ACCOUNTED_CR?
options: Entered amounts are in the transaction's entered currency; accounted amounts are converted into the ledger's functional currency
Entered amounts are always in USD
Accounted amounts only apply to manual journals
There is no difference — they are always identical
questions.explain: For a foreign-currency transaction, the entered and accounted amount pairs can differ; for a transaction already in the ledger's currency, they match.

questions.q: What does the JE_SOURCE column on GL_JE_HEADERS tell you?
options: Where the journal came from — e.g. a subledger like Payables, or a Manual/Spreadsheet entry typed directly into GL
questions.explain: JE_SOURCE distinguishes subledger-generated journals (Payables, Receivables, Assets, etc.) from journals entered directly by a person.

options: A single debit or credit line
A named group of one or more journal entries entered or imported together, with its own posting status
questions.explain: A batch groups journal entries together and is posted as a unit, with status information independent of the individual journals inside it.
